brief.summary_1line: The gods complain to Brahma about Ravana, leading Vishnu to resolve to incarnate as Dasaratha’s four sons to destroy the tyrant.

image_candidates.scene_text: The assembled gods with folded hands plead before Brahma while the radiant Vishnu, bearing conch, discus, and mace, appears in golden robes.
The gods stand in fear as they describe Ravana’s power, the sun dimmed and the wind stilled before the unseen tyrant.
Vishnu declares his vow before the gathered deities to be born as the four sons of King Dasaratha to destroy Ravana.

deep.rich_summary: King Dasaratha asks the sage Rishyasringa how he might obtain an heir. The sage promises that the king will father four sons and begins the Putrakameshti sacrifice described in the Atharva Veda. As the ritual proceeds, celestial beings gather, but they soon appeal to Brahma with a grave complaint: the rakshasa king Ravana, empowered by boons, tyrannizes the three worlds and even humiliates the gods. Brahma reveals the flaw in Ravana’s protection—he asked immunity from gods and spirits but dismissed humans as insignificant. At that moment Vishnu appears, and the gods implore him to be born as Dasaratha’s son and destroy Ravana. Vishnu agrees, vowing to incarnate as four sons of the king and end the demon’s reign, setting in motion the divine origin of Rama and his brothers.

highlight_spans.why: The opening exchange where Dasaratha seeks an heir introduces the human problem that will intersect with the divine plan.
The gods’ lament about Ravana’s oppression conveys the emotional urgency and cosmic suffering caused by the demon king.
Brahma explains the loophole in Ravana’s boon—only a human can kill him—revealing the pivotal mythic twist that drives the epic.
Vishnu’s appearance and the gods’ plea for him to incarnate marks the decisive divine intervention that leads to Rama’s birth.
Vishnu’s promise to destroy Ravana and rule on earth for eleven thousand years confirms the cosmic mission behind the coming incarnation.

top_scenes.scene_text: In a celestial assembly of gods and sages before Brahma, the devas plead desperately for relief from Ravana’s tyranny.
Vishnu appears in radiant form with conch, discus, and mace, clad in yellow robes, seated beside Brahma as the gods bow and entreat him.
The gods look on in awe as Vishnu declares he will descend to earth as the four sons of King Dasaratha to destroy Ravana.
